ashwin: quick heads up — after the new matmul kernel route landed on canary we're seeing intermittent OOMs on long-context L2-13B runs (seq 32k, batch 2). reproducer attached and a short heap trace. :frowning:

perf-bot: [auto] perf snapshot uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/1749876543/snapshot.pb · 6s profile · 17% alloc growth during kv warmup

marta: thanks. any changes to allocator knobs in the canary? max_split_size_mb / expandable_segments / gc_threshold?

ashwin: no deliberate changes in canary, defaults are in play. quick paste of the run env: 
```
MODEL=llama-2-13b
SEQ=32768
BATCH=2
GPU=A100-80GB
PT_ALLOCATOR_EXPANDABLE_SEGMENTS=1
PT_ALLOCATOR_MAX_SPLIT_SIZE_MB=32
PT_ALLOCATOR_GC_THRESHOLD=0.15
```

simon: interesting — the trace shows a lot of short-lived 8–16MB cudaMalloc/free churn around attention kv cache growth. could be fragmentation + kernel working set spike. do you have a timeline of kernel switches?

ashwin: yes — matmul kernel selector switched at t=00:00:42 to amx_v2 for large heads. before that we were on amx_v1. Attached callstack snippet in the snapshot.

lena: repro command I ran locally: `python -m repro.run --model $MODEL --seq $SEQ --batch $BATCH --trace --alloc-stats` produced an OOM at step 12 for me. paste of the alloc-stats (truncated):
```
STEP 11: used=59.3GB reserved=64GB active_allocs=1204 free_frag=4.1GB
STEP 12: cudaMalloc(18432000) -> OOM, used=64.1GB reserved=64GB
recent frees: many 16MB chunks returned ~30s prior
```

marta: garbage_collection_threshold 0.15 seems low if we keep lots of small frees. bumping to 0.4 forces earlier GC sweeps. can you test toggling that to see if fragmentation drops?

ashwin: running a quick sweep now with PT_ALLOCATOR_GC_THRESHOLD=0.4 and PT_ALLOCATOR_MAX_SPLIT_SIZE_MB=64 to allow coarser splits. queueing results.

perf-bot: [auto] experiment 1749876543-A: gc_threshold=0.4, max_split=64 · initial 10 steps complete · no OOM so far · avg alloc latency +3% · token throughput -1.8%

ashwin: ok experiment A survived to step 50 locally. alloc fragmentation report: free_frag ~10.2GB and active_allocs down 18%. behavior looks better.

simon: good signal. but we need to see if kernel choice influences peak working set. can we force the old kernel in selector and rerun? if amx_v2 creates larger temp buffers then even with less frag we might still spike.

lena: forcing old kernel is easy: set KERNEL_SELECTOR_OVERRIDE=amx_v1 in env. I ran that with original knobs and it also survived longer, OOM moved to step 80 instead of 12. looks like both factors matter.

marta: propose we run a 2x2 matrix: {kernel: amx_v1, amx_v2} x {gc_threshold: 0.15, 0.4} x fixed seeds and collect alloc profiles + batch latency distributions. we should also capture KV cache growth curve.

ashwin: agreed. I'll schedule the matrix on canary nodes tonight. small note: we should instrument continuous batching to see if batching heuristics cause temporary concurrency bumps — maybe kernel change increases per-request workspace so batching pushes us over.

simon: add a probe to log workspace peaks per request: `alloc_stats.request_peak_bytes` in SDK. correlate with batch size and kernel.

perf-bot: [auto] scheduled job: jobs/1749876543/matrix-run · ETA 2h · collecting: alloc timeline, batch-latency-p50/p95, kv-cache-size, kernel-tag

lena: one more data point — I tried increasing PT_ALLOCATOR_EXPANDABLE_SEGMENTS=0 (disable expansion to force splits) and it made fragmentation worse. expandable_segments=1 + larger max_split seems the path.

ashwin: thanks. i'll post the matrix results here and a short playbook to mitigate in prod: 1) bump gc_threshold to 0.4 on high-context SKUs, 2) increase max_split_size_mb for models > 8B, 3) conservative kernel rollouts with perf baseline.

marta: sounds good. will draft rollout notes and a canary gating test: block kernel change if avg free_frag < 6GB after warmup. :white_check_mark:

simon: also add a cheap unit-test in runtime that simulates kv warmup with many small frees and fails if fragmentation ratio exceeds threshold. helps catch regressions earlier.

ashwin: will do. thanks everyone. leaving the snapshot link and quick repro: s3://redwood-perf/1749876543/snapshot.pb · gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/repro-1749876543

perf-bot: [auto] thread closed: job complete · results uploaded · summary in jobs/1749876543/matrix-run/summary.json
